shell.authOffTip: BOARD_ENV={{env}}, sign-in off: signed in as {{actor}}. Not the live board.

defaultAgent.title: Default agent CLI
defaultAgent.text: The one <link>Connect an agent</link> opens on, showing only its commands.

previews.title: Previews
previews.text: How many previews the board builds and runs at once, in every project (1 to 32). Each is a whole board with its own copy of the data; a start beyond the limit is refused. A project's Previews page shows how many are in use.

theme.title: Theme
theme.text: Follows your system by default. The choice is kept in this browser, not on the board.

language.title: Language
language.text: The language of the whole interface, dates and numbers included. It is kept on the board, so it follows you to every device you sign in from. What people and agents write stays as it was written.

connect.browserNoCopy: The browser did not allow copying; select the text instead
connect.title: Connect an agent
connect.intro: Connect a CLI: Generate commands makes its MCP token, and the skill installs on this machine with a button (or with the line, on another machine). The default CLI is set in Settings.

step1.title: 1. Connect the MCP server
step1.command: Run once in a terminal; it registers the server for every repo.
step1.configOpencode: Add to {{file}} (merge the board entry into "mcp" if the file already has one).

step2.title: 2. Install the skill
step2.text: Downloads the board's current skill to {{path}}, where {{agent}} finds it in every repo.
step2.textCodex: Downloads the board's current skill to {{path}}, where {{agent}} finds it in every repo. OpenCode reads this folder too.
step2.textOpencode: Downloads the board's current skill to {{path}}, where {{agent}} finds it in every repo. OpenCode also reads ~/.claude/skills: skip this if Claude Code has it already.
step2.tokenNote: The install lines carry a download token that expires <time>{{at}}</time>: about ten minutes. Copy a line again after that for a new one.
step2.session: Also installs /session, the skill that opens a session with the board: it gives you a short brief, delegates every ticket you name, and keeps one message shape with what needs you.

opencode.readFailed: Could not read the OpenCode config
opencode.readFailedText: Fix that file, then check again. Multilevel delegation stays off until the config can be read.
opencode.readFrom: Read from {{source}}. The system-wide config outranks global and project files.
opencode.off: Multilevel delegation is off: subagents cannot launch subagents
opencode.offText: Add this to {{source}} (inside its experimental block if it has one), then restart OpenCode. The last config file that defines an experimental block decides; the system-wide config outranks global and project files, so a later one can override an earlier depth. The board only reads files.
opencode.deprecated: The top-level subagent_depth in {{source}} is no longer read by OpenCode; only experimental.subagent_depth counts.

generate.newOrchestrator: The commands below carry a new orchestrator token for {{name}}, valid until {{until}}. It is shown this once: copy what you need now. Leaving the page loses it; pressing again makes another.
generate.newWorker: The commands below carry a new worker token for {{name}}, valid until {{until}}. It is shown this once: copy what you need now. Leaving the page loses it; pressing again makes another.
generate.intro: Makes a token for this agent and fills it into every command on this page. It is an orchestrator by default, so it can also change the projects' instructions; make it a worker in Settings, Agent tokens. The name is the agent's name on the board. A token signs in for 1 year, unless revoked, and is shown only once.

tokens.title: Agent tokens
tokens.listText: The tokens the commands above carry, each with its role: an orchestrator, which also changes the projects' instructions, or a worker (both set in Settings, Agent tokens; a new one is an orchestrator). Revoke one and the agent using it is signed out at its next request.
tokens.revokeText: The agent using it is refused from its next request on. Generate commands again to connect it with a new one.

identities.text: Who is who: each agent token is an identity on the board, an orchestrator unless you make it a worker. Its subagents that name themselves under it are listed with it, always as workers; a long list starts folded, with an eye button for the rest.
identities.empty: No agent tokens yet: Connect an agent makes them.
identities.orchestratorTip: An orchestrator also changes the projects' instructions; each change waits in your Needs you until you review or revert it. Its subagents that say who they are (<token>/<name>) stay workers.
identities.revokeText: The agent using it, and every subagent working under it, is refused from its next request on. Generate commands again on Connect an agent to connect it with a new one.

devices.title: Devices
devices.text: The passkeys that sign in to the board. A passkey works on the address it was made on: this machine (localhost), or the board's tailnet name for your other devices.
devices.link: Open this link on the new device and create a passkey there. It works once, until {{until}}.
devices.revokeText: The passkey signs in no more, and the browsers signed in with it are signed out.

tailnet.title: Other devices (tailnet)
tailnet.text: Open the board from your other devices and cloud agents over your tailnet, with HTTPS. Turn it on here; no file to edit. Your devices then sign in with passkeys of their own (Devices, below).
tailnet.signInOff: Sign-in is off on this board (BOARD_ENV={{env}}): it answers on this machine only, never through the tailnet, so the entrance cannot be saved here.
tailnet.fromEnv: Set in config.env (or .env): PUBLIC_ORIGIN={{origin}}. It wins over this setting, so the entrance is read-only here. Remove that line there to set it in Settings.
tailnet.funnel: Tailscale Funnel is on: it puts the board on the internet, which the board refuses. Turn it off (tailscale funnel off, or tailscale serve reset); saving is refused until then.
tailnet.unserved: The saved entrance is not served: {{reason}}.
tailnet.turnOffText: The board stops answering on {{origin}}. Browsers signed in through that name are signed out (their passkeys stay listed).
tailnet.hint: Only https, a host name, no port and no path. Saved in the board's database and applied at once, without a restart.
tailnet.servedNone: Served now: nothing; the board answers on this machine only.

next.notInstalled: Tailscale is not installed on this machine: install it and sign in, then check again (README: Using it from other devices).
next.notSignedIn: Tailscale is {{state}} on this machine: run tailscale up and sign in, then check again.
next.noName: This machine has no tailnet name: turn on MagicDNS in the Tailscale admin console, then check again.
next.httpsOff: HTTPS certificates are off for {{name}}: turn them on in the Tailscale admin console, then check again.
next.ready: Ready: this machine is {{name}} on your tailnet, and serve sends it to the board.

tailnet.serveOther: Port 443 of this machine serves {{target}} now. To send https://{{name}} to the board instead, run this here:
tailnet.serveNotSet: Serve is not set up yet. To open the board at https://{{name}} run this here:
tailnet.neverRuns: The board never runs it. Then check again. To stop: tailscale serve --https=443 off.

updates.title: Updates
updates.checkout: This board runs from a checkout, which has no updater. To update it, run git pull on main in that checkout, then pnpm start (README: "Running it"). Only the desktop app checks for and installs new versions from here.
updates.unsupported: This copy of the app cannot update itself: it runs from an unpacked folder, not from its installer or a package. Install a release from GitHub to get updates here.
updates.installing: Installing {{version}}: the board stops for a moment and the app starts again as the new version.
updates.autoCheck: Check for updates at start and every six hours
updates.note: Nothing is downloaded or installed until you press Download and install. Each download is checked against the sha512 in the release's metadata first.
updates.skipped: Skipped {{version}}: the update card will not show for it again.
updates.manual: Run this in a terminal to install it, then start the app again:

skills.failedBoard: Could not install the board skill (HTTP {{status}})
skills.failedReview: Could not install the review skills (HTTP {{status}})
skills.failedBoardAria: Could not install the board skill
skills.failedReviewAria: Could not install the review skills
skills.failedHint: Check that the folder belongs to the user the board runs as, and that it can be written to.
skills.intro: /todo-review works the To do tickets to hand-off and /review-queue reviews the PR queue, both delegating to these agents. /feature-review is the review they run on each change. One line installs all three, with their agents, into ~/.claude (Claude Code; OpenCode reads its skills too), replacing files of the same name.
skills.placeholderNote: It carries {{placeholder}} until a line is copied: the board then mints a download token, good for about ten minutes, for every install line on this page.
skills.globalText: The copy in ~/.claude on the machine the board runs on, which Claude Code uses in every repo without a copy of its own. The line above brings it up to date.
skills.globalHomeText: The copy in the folder CLAUDE_HOME names on the machine the board runs on, in place of ~/.claude. The line above installs into ~/.claude: this copy has a line of its own that installs the files into that folder.
skills.noneGlobal: None of these files are there yet: the line above installs them.
skills.noneHome: None of these files are there yet: this line installs them.
skills.reposText: A repo can carry its own copy in its .claude folder, which Claude Code uses there instead of the one in ~/.claude. An outdated copy has a line that installs these files into that repo's .claude, replacing files of the same name and keeping the rest.
skills.noReposProject: No repos in this project yet.
skills.noReposBoard: No repos on the board yet.
skills.differ_one: {{count}} of {{total}} files differ or are missing
skills.differ_other: {{count}} of {{total}} files differ or are missing

skillDiff.description: What the install line would change: lines marked - are in the installed copy and go, lines marked + come from the copy the board serves. Line endings aside.
skillDiff.unreadable: The installed copy can't be read as text ({{reason}}): {{path}}
skillDiff.noChanges: No changes: the installed copy is up to date with the board's.

hostTools.dismissTip: Hide this until the next check finds {{name}} still missing
hostTools.recheckTip: Look for git, gh, claude, node and pnpm again on the board's PATH
